hook.line: Two guesses sound almost the same, and the only clue to when they happen is the ending. Mix them up and you will be guessing about the wrong day.

examples.en: It must have been about ten when he arrived.
Vale is probably in the kitchen.
Vale was probably in the kitchen.

rule:
Both forms are guesses. The ending tells you when.

*-á* (*estará*, *serán*, *tendrá*): a guess about now.
*-ía* (*estaría*, *serían*, *tendría*): a guess about then.

*Ahora Tomás estará cansado.* Tomás is probably tired.
*Anoche Tomás estaría cansado.* Tomás was probably tired.

The stems are identical (*tendr-*, *sabr-*, *habr-*), so only the ending moves. A word like *ahora*, *ayer* or *cuando llegó* usually points the way too.
smallPrint: Teachers contrast the future of probability (about the present) with the conditional of probability (about the past).

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *estará* or *estaría* and type the whole sentence: *Ahora Tomás ___ cansado.*
Pick *estará* or *estaría* and type the whole sentence: *Anoche Tomás ___ cansado.*
yourTurn.why: *Anoche* is in the past, so the *-ía* ending.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: He's probably at home.
Type in Spanish: He was probably at home.
Type in Spanish: Vale was probably in the kitchen.
Make it about now: *Habría mucha gente.* Say: There must be a lot of people.
Make it about then: *Mariana sabrá algo.* Say: Mariana probably knew something.
yourTurn.why: Then takes *-ía* on the same stem: *sabría*.

pitfalls.wrong: Ayer Vale estará en la cocina.
pitfalls.right: Ayer Vale estaría en la cocina.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Ayer* is the past, and the future ending guesses about now.
Almost. For a guess about right now, use *-á*; the *-ía* ending looks back.
Almost. The accent on the final *á* is what marks the future.

personal: Think of a friend and guess two things: what they are probably doing now (*estará*) and what they were probably doing last night (*estaría*).
